answers.answer: BoatAttack is Unity-Technologies' Unity/Universal RP demo: a small boat-racing game slice with boats and an island, intended for render-pipeline development, testing and learning. It runs in the Unity Editor or a built Unity player; it is not presented as a hosted service. The README credits Andre McGrail for design, programming, modeling, textures and SFX, Alex Best for modeling/textures and Stintah for music. The pin does not establish a current operational maintainer.

Principal runtime pieces: Boat owns per-boat setup, controller selection, lap progress, appearance and reset; HumanController translates player input, while AiController navigates waypoints/NavMesh; Engine applies propulsion/turning and samples water depth. RaceManager owns race data, spawning, countdown, standings and player UI/camera setup. MainMenuHelper configures a race; CameraManager switches Cinemachine camera modes. The local WaterSystem package supplies water/buoyancy/rendering, with separate editor tools. NavMeshComponents support navigation, and UnityGFXTests supplies graphics-test assemblies.

C# MonoBehaviours organize gameplay (BoatAttack and BoatAttack.UI); generated C# InputControls wraps an Input System JSON action asset. Rendering also uses ShaderLab/HLSL and Shader Graph. This pin specifies Unity 2020.3.23f1; Packages/manifest.json pins URP 10.7.0, Input System 1.1.1, Cinemachine 2.9.1 and Addressables 1.19.11. Embedded com.verasl.water-system is a Unity package, not evidence of a Node runtime despite the map's npm label: it has WaterSystem runtime and Editor-only WaterSystem.Editor asmdefs. NavMeshComponents likewise separates runtime/editor; graphics tests have their own test-constrained assembly. The map indexes 89 C# files; it is not exhaustive language coverage.

The documented full-play entry is scenes/main_menu.unity. MainMenuHelper.SetupSingleplayerGame calls SetGameType(Singleplayer); RaceManager marks the first BoatData human, and the menu's hull selection calls SetHull. StartRace calls LoadGame, whose sceneLoaded callback starts SetupRace/CreateBoats. Addressables instantiates the selected prefab, then Boat.Setup receives boat.human. Boat.SetupController selects typeof(HumanController) and adds it dynamically. Its Awake/OnEnable initialize input. Serialized UI event wiring and Unity lifecycle dispatch are runtime boundaries, not a proven uninterrupted static call chain.

Assets/Scripts/Boat/Engine.cs, Engine.Accelerate(float), lines 64-75. Only when _yHeight > -0.1f does it clamp modifier to [0,1], flatten and normalize Rigidbody forward, apply horsePower × modifier × forward using ForceMode.Acceleration, and add relative pitch torque. Engine.FixedUpdate computes _yHeight as sampled water height minus the transformed engine sample-point height, using GerstnerWavesJobs. Equality at -0.1 fails the gate; negative throttle is clamped to zero, not reverse thrust.

HumanController → BaseController: inheritance and base.OnEnable call. → InputControls: constructs it, subscribes action callbacks and enables/disables BoatControls. → Boat: inherited controller.ResetPosition call. → Engine: inherited engine.Accelerate/Turn calls. → DayNightController: static SelectPreset call. BaseController resolves the Boat component and obtains controller.engine. These directions are proven by source expressions/types; the map's empty outgoing call list does not prove no dependencies.

Held positive throttle follows the Trottle input action through Input System callback dispatch to stored _throttle, then Unity's recurring HumanController.FixedUpdate calls Engine.Accelerate. The engine's independently scheduled FixedUpdate samples water; Accelerate gates on that stored depth and applies Rigidbody acceleration. Holding retains the last value; canceled resets it. Dynamic boundaries are input-event dispatch, Unity lifecycle/FixedUpdate scheduling, component creation/reference wiring, water-job sampling and native physics integration. Source inspection establishes this supported path, not callback ordering or observed motion.

Two evidenced direct consumers are HumanController.FixedUpdate, passing _throttle, and AiController.FixedUpdate, passing dot > 0 ? 1f : 0.25f after its path guard. Changes to Engine.Accelerate semantics therefore affect both player and AI propulsion. Boat/RaceManager are upstream setup components, not evidenced direct Accelerate callers. This is a source-confirmed consumer set, not a completeness guarantee from the map: even includeEstimated=true returned zero incoming edges.

README documents scenes/demo_island.unity as the editor-ready AI race example; this exercises acceleration via AiController.FixedUpdate → Engine.Accelerate. For human acceleration it documents scenes/main_menu.unity for a full play-through and scenes/_levels/level_Island.unity as the loaded level. The supported code entry is menu singleplayer setup/load → RaceManager.SetupRace/CreateBoats → Boat.Setup/SetupController → HumanController. The README does not supply an isolated throttle unit-test example. Scene/prefab serialized wiring and actual execution were not verified.

Z enters in Assets/Data/InputControls.inputactions as BoatControls/Trottle (spelling preserved), an Axis Value action with AxisDeadzone(min=0.1,max=1). Its 1DAxis composite combines negative left-trigger/buttonEast/down/S/Z and positive right-trigger/buttonSouth/up/W/space bindings; touch-position Y has Clamp(-1,1). Generated InputControls constructs the action asset. HumanController reads a float on performed, stores it, and clears it on canceled; FixedUpdate forwards it. Engine clamps again to [0,1], scales by horsepower and the horizontal forward direction, subject to the water gate. Device dispatch/processor internals belong to the external Input System.
